symptom: Every create microflow / create nanoflow / alter microflow on a Mendix 9.x project failed after earlier statements had already been written: "this Mendix 9.24.2 project cannot store Microflows$Microflow.StableId (Mendix 10.2.0+); Microflows$SequenceFlow.CaseValues (Mendix 10.15.0+)" (10.0-10.14: CaseValues alone), while `mxcli check` passed the script
cause: The flow writers emitted the newest shape whatever the version, gated by major at most: StableId as an unconditional FreshGUIDFields codec default (10.2+), the case always as a CaseValues list (10.15+), always a BezierCurve Line (10.16+), ReturnVariableName and parameter IsRequired/DefaultValue on any 10.x (10.12+ / 10.17+). The property floor added on 2026-10-10 started refusing the two that held a value; before it they were written silently, and on 9.24 the case list is not read at all (forced back in: 8 errors, CE0079/CE0773). Line, LineType, ReturnVariableName and the parameter keys were never refused because the floor looks a key up on the element's own $Type only and these are declared on supertypes (Flow, MicroflowBase) or under another $Type (MicroflowParameterObject). And gen bound the single case under its SDK name "CaseValue"; Studio Pro stores it as "NewCaseValue"
file: `mdl/backend/modelsdk/microflow_write.go` (flowVersion, microflowEncoder, sequenceFlowToGen, annotationFlowToGen, microflowParameterToGen), `nanoflow_write.go`, `rule_write.go`, `microflow_mutator_write.go`, `microflow_readback.go`, `microflow.go` (flowsFromGen reads the bezier vectors), `modelsdk/gen/microflows/types.go` (initSequenceFlow storage-name override), `modelsdk/codec/encoder.go` (OmitKeys applies to registered defaults)
insight: Get the old shape from a real document, not the gen: dump a Studio Pro-authored 9.x flow (any marketplace module's microflow with a decision) and run `mx convert -p` to a mid-10 version (10.12.19 here) to get a Studio Pro-serialized document for that version for free — its key sets settle LineType (10.8-10.15 only), NewCaseValue, StableId and the absent parameter keys in one dump, and mxcli's output can be diffed key-set for key-set against it. The floor (canon.StripUndeclaredProperties) is a backstop, not a gate: it cannot see supertype-declared keys, so a writer clean under the floor can still write keys the version lacks — check the Model SDK's versionInfo for the type AND its supertypes. A refusal at exec time leaves earlier statements written; #1434 (check is not version-aware) is the same root cause and is cured by the writer emitting a storable shape, not by teaching check the floor.
